issues.description: Method return type mismatch for Lecture.toString(): the problem statement and UML/example describe toString() as returning a String, but the solution implementation declares "public Object toString()" with an @Override annotation. Because Object.toString() has signature public String toString(), the solution's signature does not match and the @Override will produce a compilation error. This contradicts the expected String return type and will confuse or block students who rely on the correct toString() signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the solution implementation to declare the method as an overriding toString that returns String: use "@Override" followed by "public String toString()" and ensure the method returns a String. Update the solution code (and any instructor notes) so the implemented signature matches the problem statement and the Java Object.toString() signature to avoid compilation errors.
